notes.front: What is Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform?
notes.back: Google Cloud's unified platform for building, deploying, governing and optimising enterprise AI agents and model-based solutions; it evolved from Vertex AI.
notes.explanation: It covers the whole AI lifecycle, from reaching over 200 foundation models to deploying and managing agents.
notes.example: Like a workshop, a warehouse and a quality office under one roof: you design agents, run them and inspect them in the same place.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Platform overview”, introduction
notes.evidence: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is a unified platform to build, deploy, govern, and optimize enterprise-grade AI agents and model-based solutions. As an evolution of Vertex AI, it supports the complete AI lifecycle from accessing over 200 foundation models to deploying and managing your agents.

notes.front: What is the Agent Platform API, according to the study guide?
notes.back: A pre-trained Google Cloud interface (API) for building, orchestrating and governing autonomous enterprise AI agents.
notes.explanation: The study guide lists it first among Google Cloud's pre-trained interfaces.
notes.example: Like a switchboard that your own software rings to set agents to work, rather than a screen a person clicks through.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence”, p. 7
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Cloud Vision API?
notes.back: A Google Cloud API that analyses images; for example, its text detection recognises text in an image and converts it to machine-coded text.
notes.explanation: Text detection is optical character recognition: turning pictures of words into text a computer can work with.
notes.example: Like a fast reader looking at a photo of a shop sign and typing out what it says.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud Vision API “Features list”, “Text detection”
notes.evidence: Optical character recognition (OCR) for an image; text recognition and conversion to machine-coded text.

notes.front: What is the Cloud Translation API?
notes.back: A Google Cloud API that lets websites and applications translate text with Google's translation models, programmatically.
notes.explanation: ‘Programmatically’ means that software calls the translation models directly.
notes.example: Like a translator built into your website's plumbing, turning each page into the visitor's language as it is served.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Google translation offerings”
notes.evidence: Google Cloud translation offerings enable your websites and applications to translate text with state-of-the-art translation models. Depending on your use case, you can use the Cloud Translation API to apply those models programmatically

notes.front: What is Speech-to-Text?
notes.back: A Google Cloud API that lets developers build Google's speech recognition into their own applications, turning spoken audio into text.
notes.explanation: The study guide sums it up as converting spoken audio into accurate written text.
notes.example: Like a stenographer inside your app, writing down every word a caller says.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Cloud Speech-to-Text overview”, introduction
notes.evidence: Cloud Speech-to-Text is an API that lets you integrate Google's speech recognition technologies into your developer applications.

notes.front: What is Gemini, in Google Cloud's generative AI documentation?
notes.back: Google's family of generative AI models built for multimodal use, able to process images, videos and text.
notes.explanation: The study guide calls Gemini Google's advanced multimodal reasoning and generation model.
notes.example: Like a colleague you can show a photo, a clip and a note to, and ask one question about all three.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Generative AI beginner's guide”, introduction
notes.evidence: Google provides the Gemini family of generative AI models designed for multimodal use cases; capable of processing information from multiple modalities, including images, videos, and text.

notes.front: What is Model Garden?
notes.back: A central place on Agent Platform to discover, test and deploy many models: Google's own, partners' and open-source ones.
notes.explanation: It gathers models from several makers in one catalogue.
notes.example: Like a large library where one catalogue lists books from many publishers, including free ones.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Overview of models on Agent Platform”, “Model Garden”
notes.evidence: Model Garden provides a centralized location to discover, test, and deploy a wide variety of first-party, partner, and open-source models.

notes.front: What is a foundation model on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform?
notes.back: One of the ready-made generative AI models, such as Gemini, that the platform offers through a managed API.
notes.explanation: The models differ in size, modality and cost; Google, open and partner models can be explored in Model Garden.
notes.example: Like a trained, general-purpose engine you bolt into your product, instead of building an engine from scratch.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Generative AI beginner's guide”, “Foundation models”
notes.evidence: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform has a variety of generative AI foundation models that are accessible through a managed API, including the following: - Gemini API: Advanced reasoning, multiturn chat, code generation, and multimodal prompts. The models differ in size, modality, and cost. You can explore Google models, as well as open models and models from Google partners, in Model Garden.

notes.front: What is Agent Studio?
notes.back: A shared workspace on Agent Platform for discovering models, refining system instructions and optimising prompts; it was formerly Vertex AI Studio.
notes.explanation: It helps turn ideas into production-ready generative AI solutions.
notes.example: Like a test kitchen where you try recipes and adjust seasoning before a dish goes on the restaurant menu.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Studio overview”, introduction
notes.evidence: Agent Studio provides a centralized, collaborative workspace for discovering models, refining system instructions, and optimizing prompts. By integrating built-in experiences with the broader Google Cloud ecosystem, Agent Studio helps you transform innovative ideas into production-ready generative AI solutions.

notes.front: What is AutoML on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform?
notes.back: The platform's fast path to high-quality ML models, as an alternative to building custom models with frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch.
notes.explanation: Both routes run on the same platform, which manages the whole ML lifecycle.
notes.example: Like a bread machine: you add your own ingredients and it handles the kneading and baking you would otherwise do by hand.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to machine learning on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform”
notes.evidence: Whether you are using AutoML for a fast path to high-quality models or creating custom models with popular frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch, Agent Platform operationalizes the entire ML lifecycle.

notes.front: What is a Tensor Processing Unit (TPU)?
notes.back: A chip Google custom-developed (an application-specific integrated circuit) to accelerate machine learning workloads.
notes.explanation: Application-specific means built for one kind of job: here, speeding up ML.
notes.example: Like a machine built only to press one shape of part: far faster at that job than a general-purpose lathe.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”
notes.evidence: Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) are Google's custom-developed, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) used to accelerate machine learning workloads.

notes.front: What are graphics processing units (GPUs) used for on Google Cloud?
notes.back: Accelerating machine learning, data processing and graphics-intensive workloads on Google Cloud machines.
notes.explanation: Machine learning is only one of the jobs they speed up; data processing and graphics work are others.
notes.example: Like adding a team of fast specialist helpers to a computer for jobs that split into many small, similar calculations.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “GPU machine types”, introduction
notes.evidence: GPU models that you can use to accelerate machine learning (ML), data processing, and graphics-intensive workloads

notes.front: What is AI Hypercomputer?
notes.back: Google Cloud's integrated supercomputing system for AI and ML workloads, bringing its AI hardware, open software and consumption models together.
notes.explanation: It is the unified portfolio for all of Google Cloud's AI infrastructure.
notes.example: Like a racing team that tunes the engine, the software and the fuel budget together, rather than buying parts separately.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “AI Hypercomputer overview”, introduction
notes.evidence: AI Hypercomputer is an integrated supercomputing system that's optimized to support your artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) workloads. It is the unified portfolio for Google Cloud's AI infrastructure

notes.front: What is BigQuery ML?
notes.back: A BigQuery feature for creating and running ML models with GoogleSQL queries or the Google Cloud console.
notes.explanation: Its models are stored in BigQuery datasets, like tables and views.
notes.example: Like a spreadsheet that can learn to forecast, using the same formulas the analysts already write.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to ML in BigQuery”
notes.evidence: BigQuery ML lets you create and run machine learning (ML) models by using either GoogleSQL queries or the Google Cloud console. BigQuery ML models are stored in BigQuery datasets, similar to tables and views.

notes.front: How does Agent Platform cater for both low-code and code-based developers?
notes.back: Low-code: Agent Studio, to design agents without code. Code-based: Colab Enterprise notebooks and the Agent Development Kit.
notes.explanation: The platform aims to meet teams where they are, with tools for all skill levels.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Platform overview”, introduction
notes.evidence: Agent Platform meets you where you are, with tools for all skill levels: - Low-code development: - Agent Studio: Design agents and interact with models without code.

notes.front: Which Agent Platform pillar covers designing, prototyping and developing AI agents?
notes.back: Build.
notes.explanation: The platform is organised around four pillars: Build, Scale, Govern and Optimize.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Platform overview”, “Components”
notes.evidence: Use these tools and services to design, prototype, and develop your AI agents.

notes.front: Which Agent Platform pillar covers deploying and managing agents in a high-performance runtime?
notes.back: Scale.
notes.explanation: The platform is organised around four pillars: Build, Scale, Govern and Optimize.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Platform overview”, “Components”
notes.evidence: Deploy and manage your agents in a high-performance, stateful runtime environment.

notes.front: Which Agent Platform pillar covers securing and cataloguing agents with enterprise controls and policies?
notes.back: Govern.
notes.explanation: The platform is organised around four pillars: Build, Scale, Govern and Optimize.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Platform overview”, “Components”
notes.evidence: Secure, catalog, and govern your agents with enterprise-grade controls and policies.

notes.front: Which Agent Platform pillar covers assessing, monitoring and refining agents for quality and reliability?
notes.back: Optimize.
notes.explanation: The platform is organised around four pillars: Build, Scale, Govern and Optimize.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Platform overview”, “Components”
notes.evidence: Assess, monitor, and refine your agents to ensure high quality and reliability.

notes.front: Which Cloud Vision API feature suits scanned document files and handwriting?
notes.back: Document text detection, which is optimised for dense text, document files and handwriting.
notes.explanation: It accepts document files as well as images.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud Vision API “Features list”, “Document text detection”
notes.evidence: Files: Optimized for document files (PDF/TIFF). - Images: Optimized for dense areas of text in an image (images that are documents), and images that contain handwriting.

notes.front: How does Cloud Translation – Basic differ from Cloud Translation – Advanced?
notes.back: Basic gives quick, plug-and-play access to the standard neural machine translation model; Advanced adds an advanced translation large language model.
notes.explanation: So Advanced is the edition to choose when you want the translation large language model; both editions give access to the standard neural model.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Google translation offerings”
notes.evidence: Cloud Translation - Basic API provides quick, plug-and-play access to the standard Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model. - Cloud Translation - Advanced API provides access to an advanced Translation LLM (TLLM) model and the standard Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model.

notes.front: Which Speech-to-Text recognition method suits live audio from a microphone?
notes.back: Streaming recognition, which returns interim results while the audio is still being captured.
notes.explanation: Results can appear while the person is still speaking.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Cloud Speech-to-Text overview”, “Recognition requests”
notes.evidence: Streaming requests are designed for real-time recognition purposes, such as capturing live audio from a microphone. Streaming recognition provides interim results as audio is captured. For example, results can appear while a user is still speaking.

notes.front: How do synchronous and asynchronous Speech-to-Text requests differ in the audio they handle?
notes.back: Synchronous requests handle audio of 1 minute or less; asynchronous requests handle audio of any length up to 480 minutes.
notes.explanation: Asynchronous requests start a long-running operation that you poll for results.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Cloud Speech-to-Text overview”, “Recognition requests”
notes.evidence: Synchronous recognition requests process audio data of 1 minute or less. - Asynchronous recognition (REST and gRPC) sends audio data to the Cloud Speech-to-Text API and initiates a long-running operation. Using this operation, you can periodically poll for recognition results. Use asynchronous requests for audio data of any duration up to 480 minutes.

notes.front: What is a multimodal model?
notes.back: A model that works with several kinds of data, such as text, images, videos and audio.
notes.explanation: Which modalities a model handles depends on the data it was trained on.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Generative AI beginner's guide”, introduction
notes.evidence: However, depending on the data that the models are trained on, these models can understand and generate content from multiple modalities, including text, images, videos, and audio. Models that work with multiple modalities of data are called multimodal models.

notes.front: What are two of the Google-developed model families that Agent Platform offers?
notes.back: Any two of: Gemini, Gemma, Veo and Lyria.
notes.explanation: These are Google's flagship families; Gemini is the one the study guide names.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Overview of models on Agent Platform”, “Model types”
notes.evidence: Flagship models developed by Google, including Gemini, Gemma, Veo, and Lyria.

notes.front: What is model tuning, for a foundation model?
notes.back: Customising the model's default behaviour so that it consistently gives the results you want without complex prompts.
notes.explanation: Simpler prompts in turn reduce the cost and latency of requests.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Generative AI beginner's guide”, “Model customization”
notes.evidence: You can customize the default behavior of Google's foundation models so that they consistently generate the desired results without using complex prompts. This customization process is called model tuning. Model tuning helps you reduce the cost and latency of your requests by allowing you to simplify your prompts.

notes.front: According to the study guide, how does Agent Studio help an organisation build agents on its own data?
notes.back: By grounding foundation models in the organisation's proprietary data, designing the operating logic visually and integrating APIs.
notes.explanation: This lets business agents automate complex workflows using what the company alone knows.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence”, p. 7
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Agent Studio, how can you improve the accuracy of an agent's responses with data?
notes.back: Ground the agent in real-time data from Google Search and Google Maps, or in your own enterprise data.
notes.explanation: Your own enterprise data can come in through Agent Search or Elasticsearch, among others.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Agent Studio overview”, “Key capabilities”
notes.evidence: Enhance response accuracy by grounding agents in real-time data from Google Search and Google Maps, or integrate your own enterprise data using RAG Engine, Agent Search, or Elasticsearch.

notes.front: Which kind of Agent Platform training requires a managed dataset: AutoML or custom training?
notes.back: AutoML. Managed datasets are required for AutoML and optional for custom training.
notes.explanation: A managed dataset supplies the source data that the model is trained on.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to machine learning on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform”, “Data preparation”
notes.evidence: Managed datasets allow you to provide source data for training models. They are required for AutoML and optional for custom training.

notes.front: Which AI Hypercomputer component provides accelerators (GPUs and TPUs), networking and storage?
notes.back: Performance-optimised infrastructure.
notes.explanation: It is one of the three components AI Hypercomputer integrates, beside open software and consumption options.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “AI Hypercomputer overview”, “System architecture”
notes.evidence: Performance-optimized infrastructure: provides accelerators (NVIDIA GPUs and Google Cloud TPUs), networking, and storage resources.

notes.front: Which AI Hypercomputer component offers optimised versions of ML frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow?
notes.back: Open software.
notes.explanation: The study guide stresses that AI Hypercomputer combines its hardware with open software standards.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “AI Hypercomputer overview”, “System architecture”
notes.evidence: Open software: offers optimized versions of machine learning frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow) and orchestration platforms.

notes.front: Which AI Hypercomputer component offers flexible ways to provision resources to suit each workload?

notes.front: What is goodput, which AI Hypercomputer is designed to maximise?
notes.back: The measure of actual machine learning productivity.
notes.explanation: Maximising it means accelerators spend more time on productive computation and less on system overhead.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “AI Hypercomputer overview”, “Benefits”
notes.evidence: High performance and goodput: optimize the scheduling and runtime layers to maximize goodput, helping accelerators spend more time on productive computation and less time on system overhead.

notes.front: What makes TPUs efficient at training ML models?
notes.back: Hardware designed for the large matrix operations often found in ML algorithms, plus on-chip high-bandwidth memory for larger models and batches.
notes.explanation: The on-chip memory lets you use larger models and batch sizes.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”
notes.evidence: TPUs efficiently train your models by using hardware designed for performing large matrix operations often found in machine learning algorithms. TPUs have on-chip high-bandwidth memory (HBM) letting you use larger models and batch sizes.

notes.front: What are TPU slices?
notes.back: Groups of connected TPUs that scale up your workloads with little to no code changes.
notes.explanation: Slices let one workload spread across many TPUs rather than one.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”
notes.evidence: TPUs can be connected in groups called slices that scale up your workloads with little to no code changes.

notes.front: According to Google's guidance, which workloads suit TPUs rather than GPUs or central processing units (CPUs)?
notes.back: Models dominated by matrix computations, models that train for weeks or months, and large models with large effective batch sizes.
notes.explanation: Models with no custom operations inside the main training loop also suit TPUs.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”, “When to use TPUs”
notes.evidence: Models dominated by matrix computations - Models with no custom PyTorch/JAX operations inside the main training loop - Models that train for weeks or months - Large models with large effective batch sizes

notes.front: How does BigQuery ML democratise ML and AI?
notes.back: It lets data analysts, the main data warehouse users, build and run models with their existing BI tools and spreadsheets.
notes.explanation: Predictive analytics can then guide business decisions across the organisation.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to ML in BigQuery”, “Advantages”
notes.evidence: BigQuery ML democratizes the use of ML and AI by empowering data analysts, the primary data warehouse users, to build and run models using existing business intelligence tools and spreadsheets. Predictive analytics can guide business decision-making across the organization.

notes.front: Which language do BigQuery ML users train models with, instead of programming in Python or Java?
notes.back: Structured Query Language, which data analysts already know.
notes.explanation: Using a familiar language removes the need to write an ML solution in Python or Java.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to ML in BigQuery”, “Advantages”
notes.evidence: You don't need to program an ML or AI solution using Python or Java. You train models and access AI resources by using SQL—a language that's familiar to data analysts.

notes.front: Why does BigQuery ML speed up model development?
notes.back: It brings ML to the data, so data does not have to be moved out of the data warehouse.
notes.explanation: Fewer tools are needed, and large amounts of data need not be moved and reformatted for Python-based frameworks.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to ML in BigQuery”, “Advantages”
notes.evidence: BigQuery ML increases the speed of model development and innovation by removing the need to move data from the data warehouse. Instead, BigQuery ML brings ML to the data, which offers the following advantages: - Reduced complexity because fewer tools are required.

notes.front: A telecoms firm's data analysts know Structured Query Language but not Python. They want to predict which customers will leave, using data already in BigQuery. Which offering fits best?
notes.back: B) BigQuery ML
notes.choices:
A) AI Hypercomputer
B) BigQuery ML
C) Cloud Vision API
D) Speech-to-Text
notes.choicesExplained: A) AI Hypercomputer is infrastructure for large AI workloads, not a query-based tool for analysts. C) Vision analyses images, not customer records. D) Speech-to-Text transcribes audio.
notes.explanation: BigQuery ML lets analysts build models with queries where the data already sits; churn prediction is the study guide's use case for it.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence”, p. 7
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A research lab needs to train a very large model for weeks on thousands of accelerators, with open frameworks and a way to control what it spends. Which offering fits best?
notes.back: B) AI Hypercomputer
notes.choices:
A) Agent Studio
B) AI Hypercomputer
C) Cloud Translation API
D) BigQuery ML
notes.choicesExplained: A) Agent Studio is a workspace for prompts and agents, not large-scale training infrastructure. C) Translation is a ready-made language service. D) BigQuery ML trains models inside a data warehouse, not on thousands of accelerators.
notes.explanation: Supercomputing workloads are the study guide's use case for AI Hypercomputer, which combines GPUs and TPUs with open software and flexible consumption.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence”, p. 7
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A bank wants an assistant that answers staff questions using the bank's own policy documents and then triggers follow-up tasks in its systems. Which offering is built for this?
notes.back: C) Agent Studio on Agent Platform
notes.choices:
A) Cloud Vision API
B) Speech-to-Text
C) Agent Studio on Agent Platform
D) Cloud Translation API
notes.choicesExplained: A) Vision reads images; it does not answer questions from policies. B) Speech-to-Text only transcribes. D) Translation converts language but cannot ground answers in the bank's own documents.
notes.explanation: The study guide describes Agent Studio as grounding foundation models in proprietary data and integrating APIs to automate workflows.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence”, p. 7
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A retailer's leaders say: “We have no ML specialists, and we can't afford a year of training before we start.” Which selection factor are they mainly weighing?
notes.back: A) Technical expertise requirements
notes.choices:
A) Technical expertise requirements
B) Potential for business differentiation
C) Choice and flexibility
D) Development effort
notes.choicesExplained: B) Differentiation is about how unique the model must be. C) Choice and flexibility is about customisation versus managed services. D) Development effort is about problem complexity and available data.
notes.explanation: Whether staff need upskilling and training is the technical expertise factor.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence”, p. 7
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A team is training a huge recommendation model, dominated by matrix maths, that will run for weeks with very large batch sizes. According to Google's guidance, which hardware suits it best?
notes.back: D) TPUs
notes.choices:
A) Central processing units (CPUs)
B) GPUs, because the model needs many custom operations on CPUs
C) A single small general-purpose machine
D) TPUs
notes.choicesExplained: A) CPUs suit quick prototyping and simple models. B) The model has no such custom operations, which is the case that points to GPUs. C) A single small machine could not train a huge model for weeks efficiently.
notes.explanation: Google lists matrix-heavy models, long training runs and large batch sizes as TPU workloads.
notes.source: Google Cloud documentation, “Introduction to Cloud TPU”, “When to use TPUs”
notes.evidence: Models dominated by matrix computations - Models with no custom PyTorch/JAX operations inside the main training loop - Models that train for weeks or months - Large models with large effective batch sizes
